def merge_intervals(intervals):
    """Merge a list of closed integer intervals (start, end).
    Touching intervals, e.g. (1,3) and (3,5), merge into (1,5).
    Input may be unsorted. Returns a sorted list of tuples."""
    if not intervals:
        return []
    # Sort intervals by start so unsorted input is handled
    sorted_intervals = sorted((tuple(i) for i in intervals), key=lambda x: x[0])
    merged = [sorted_intervals[0]]
    for start, end in sorted_intervals[1:]:
        last_start, last_end = merged[-1]
        # Merge if intervals overlap or touch (closed intervals)
        if start <= last_end:
            merged[-1] = (last_start, max(last_end, end))
        else:
            merged.append((start, end))
    return merged

arguments.summary: Fixed merge_intervals to merge touching closed intervals and handle unsorted input. Added sorting of intervals and changed merge condition to start <= last_end so (1,3) and (3,5) merge. Preserved empty input handling and returned sorted merged list.
